w-33:
Build a single-file HTML landing hero, no libraries.

Background: a full-screen <canvas> running a raw WebGL2 fragment shader. Draw soft grey bands that drift sideways in one direction only, never back. Use value noise with 3-octave fbm, warp the coordinates once, and mix three greys: ink #121212, dark band #3A3A3A, light band #C9C9C9. Make the bands thickest around 30% from the left. Add a little film grain that changes every frame. Cap devicePixelRatio at 1.5. If WebGL2 is missing, show the plain ink background.

Layer on top: a dark radial veil, a top nav (small square mark, wordmark, Work, About, and a white pill button "Book a call"), and one centered column with the headline "Make room for growth." in a serif display face (Fraunces, weight 500, tight tracking, "for growth." in italic), two short sub lines, and a pill button "See the system". A small mono caption bottom left reads "Aurora study 01".

Rules: the hero fits one screen at 390px wide, the headline fills at least 92% of the width on a phone, no autoplay audio, no hover transforms. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by freezing the shader on one frame while every control still works. Set window.__ready = true when the first frame is drawn.
w-34:
Build a single-file HTML app called "JTL Studio", no libraries, one WebGL2 canvas.

Layout: a top bar (title, a label "Preset: <name>", an Export button), a left column of three preset rows, a centered live render pane, and a right column of controls.

Presets, each a fragment shader in its own <script type="x-shader/x-fragment">: Silk (layered sine noise drifting sideways), Eclipse (a dark disc with a thin bright rim, a corona and three slow flares, rotating), Grain (fine animated grain). Each preset row shows a 64x36 thumbnail that renders the same shader. Selecting a preset swaps the program; no page reload.

Controls, all native range inputs with a numeric readout: Contrast (0 to 1, default 0.5), Grain (0 to 1, 0.15), Vignette (0 to 1, 0.35), Speed (0 to 2, 0.6), Scale (0.2 to 3, 1). Pass them as uniforms. Palette is two colors only, ink #121212 and paper #E2E2E2, mixed by luminance.

A "Copy GLSL" button copies the active fragment shader to the clipboard and confirms in place. The render pane carries a "LIVE RENDER" tag and the caption "The universe, exhaling." Respect prefers-reduced-motion by freezing time while the sliders keep working. Make it usable at 390px wide by stacking the columns.
w-35:
Build a single-file HTML product page with three.js r167 (ES module via an import map). White background, no other library.

Scene: a product made of four stacked glass parts, top to bottom: a cover disc with three rings of small dark dots, a driver (a short cylinder with a hemisphere dome), a hollow body cylinder with one thin dark seam strip so rotation is visible, and a base with a torus ring. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial (transmission 0.9, roughness 0.15, ior 1.4) in light grey and draw crisp EdgesGeometry outlines in #181818 on every part. ACES tone mapping, one ambient light, a key and a fill directional light, pixel ratio capped at 1.5.

Controls: OrbitControls with damping, no pan, a limited polar angle. A labelled range input "Explode" (0 to 1, default 0.7) moves the parts apart vertically; gaps scale with part height. Three HTML callouts ("01 Acoustic cover", "02 The driver", "03 Weighted base") are tied to their parts by thin SVG lines that follow the projected 3D position.

Page: top nav (square mark, "JTL Growth", Work, About, a pill "Book a call"), a left column with the headline "Growth. Inside out." (second line italic serif), the sub line "Four parts. One system. Every part visible.", a pill button, and the Explode slider. Caption at the bottom: "Drag to turn. Select a part." Respect prefers-reduced-motion. Phone: stack the text above the canvas.
w-36:
Build a single-file HTML portfolio page with three.js r167 (ES module via an import map).

Scene: a retro desk device seen from above at an angle: a wide low body (about 3.4 x 2.0 x 0.5 units), a large knob with tick marks on its top, a small white LED (never red) and a label plate. Matte greys and off-white only, soft shadows.

Interaction: the knob has seven detents, each (2 x PI) / 7 apart. Dragging the knob, the mouse wheel, the left and right arrow keys (page-wide) and two on-screen arrow buttons all move it one detent at a time and snap to the nearest one. It only ever turns toward the next piece with an eased motion; it never rebounds.

Content: seven pieces, each with a title and a one-line sub, shown in a copy column beside the device with a counter ("01 / 07") and an "Explore this piece" link. The text changes on every detent with a short fade. Give the device wrapper role="slider" with aria-valuemin 1, aria-valuemax 7 and aria-valuenow kept in sync, and a hidden list of the seven links for no-JS and screen readers.

Top nav: Work, Pieces, About. Hint text under the device: "Turn the dial or use your arrow keys". Respect prefers-reduced-motion by jumping between detents with no easing. On a phone, put the copy under the device and keep the buttons at least 44px.
w-37:
Build a single-file HTML logo maker called "Forme", inline SVG only, no libraries and no WebGL.

Layout: a header with the title and three buttons (Save, Copy SVG, Export as the solid one), a slim left toolbar of six icon buttons (pen, rectangle, ellipse, type, layers, download; use Lucide icon paths and keep the ISC license note in a comment), a large square canvas in the middle, and a right panel with three tabs: Form, Material, Space.

Form tab: twelve selectable shapes (circle, square, rounded square, pill, ring, quarter arc, hexagon, triangle, diamond, star, octagon, pentagon). Material tab: a Weight slider (1 to 12) that changes stroke thickness. Space tab: Rotation (0 to 360), Padding (three steps with tick marks) and a Contour switch that turns every fill into an outline. Show nine small variations under the canvas; clicking one loads it into the canvas.

Everything is one SVG group with a 24 x 24 viewBox so Copy SVG writes a clean, standalone SVG to the clipboard. Black and white only, currentColor everywhere. Tabs follow the ARIA tab pattern (arrow keys). Respect prefers-reduced-motion. Stack the panel under the canvas at 390px wide. Add window.__demo() that cycles four forms, then the weight, then turns Contour on.
w-38:
Build a single-file HTML page called "Identity studies", plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no libraries.

Generate fictional brands from a seed. Read the seed once from the query string (default 7). Use a small deterministic PRNG (mulberry32) so the same seed and index always give the same name and mark. A name is two short syllable or word parts joined and capitalised, with a blocklist so nothing real or rude appears. A mark is a simple geometric symbol built from two or three SVG primitives in black on white.

Page: a header ("Identity studies", sub "Logo gallery", a "New batch" button that changes the seed) and an infinite grid of cells, each a mark with its name. Append more rows when a sentinel at the bottom enters view (IntersectionObserver). A footer says "Fictional studies. Seed 7."

Clicking a cell opens a <dialog> brand sheet: large mark and name, a stacked lockup, a repeating brand pattern tile, a small-scale study (the mark at 48, 32, 24 and 16 px), a pack card and an app card mock, and a "Download symbol SVG" button that saves the mark as a standalone SVG with a polite status message. Never put user text through innerHTML.

Black and white, one sans-serif face. Cells need 44px tap targets. Respect prefers-reduced-motion. Add window.__demo() that scrolls three steps and opens one sheet.
w-39:
Build a single-file HTML kinetic type film, 15 seconds long, no libraries, rendered from a pure function render(t) so any time can be previewed and screenshotted.

Look: two flat grounds only, cement #E2E2E2 and ink #121212, with a 2vw ink bar down each edge. Type is Archivo ExtraBold, uppercase, tight tracking, one word placed top left and the second bottom right of each plate.

Copy lives in one array: ["FEEL THE FLOW", "BEND THE RULES", "MOVE FAST", "MAKE WAVES"]. Timeline: a 3.3 s cold open on "MOVE FAST" over cement, then three 2.0 s plates and a final plate that holds to 15.0 s. Each plate flips the ground (ink, cement, ink, cement), wipes in over 0.4 s and wipes out over 0.4 s with a clip-path. The wipe always travels left to right and never reverses. Avoid placing a cut exactly on a whole-second mark.

Controls: a centered pill "Play" that starts the clock and hides itself, no autoplay. With prefers-reduced-motion, skip the timeline and show the four lines as stacked static plates. Set window.__ready = true when fonts load and expose window.__demo(). The page must work at 390px wide with the words scaled to the viewport.
w-40:
Build a single-file HTML scene with three.js r167 (import map, ES module): a glass globe on a short wide pedestal, holding a miniature night-time street block. Everything is built from primitives, no model files.

Inside the globe: a dark ground disc with a kerb ring and a dashed road stripe, two low houses with pitched roofs (a three-sided prism squashed to the pitch), one corner shop (body, awning, a plain signboard, a counter), a bench against the front, a small van and a three-wheeler as flat silhouettes, and a lamp post with an emissive bulb, a soft halo and the scene's one point light. Palette is matte cement and ink greys, no hue anywhere.

The glass: MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission, lit by RoomEnvironment through PMREMGenerator so it reads as glass (rim streaks, refracted interior) and not a grey balloon. Cap the pixel ratio at 1.5; if the frame rate drops, lower to 1.25, then replace transmission with a 0.3 opacity.

Motion: the globe group yaws slowly in one direction forever. Dragging or pressing the left and right arrow keys only adds to that speed, never reverses it. The pedestal does not turn. Fixed three-quarter camera, slightly above, the globe centered about 55% across. Caption: "A block, after hours. Turns one way, forever." Give the stage role="img" with a descriptive aria-label, and freeze the turn under prefers-reduced-motion.
w-31:
Build a scroll-driven scene page: plain HTML, CSS and ES modules, no framework and no bundler. Files: index.html, scene.css, scene.js and data.js.

Mechanism: a tall empty #track (460vh) and a sticky full-viewport #stage. Scrolling produces one number, progress = clamp(-track.top / (trackHeight - innerHeight), 0, 1). Everything reads that number: four parallax image planes (a still cut into four luminance layers, each moved by transform at a different speed), the content slots, and a "Journey" range slider that is also the way to move for anyone who cannot scroll. Smooth the value toward the target (damping 2.2 on desktop, 5.5 on touch) before writing to the DOM, so motion glides and never snaps.

Content: data.js is the only file a client edits. It holds the scene title, an optional music URL and three slots (image, title, message, and a track). A track is a list of keyframes {at, x, y, w, h, opacity} in viewport percent, so one authored path survives 375px and 1280px. Opening a slot shows a memory card dialog with the image, the title and the message.

Gates: a first "Explore in full screen?" dialog and a "Start this walk with sound?" dialog, since browsers block autoplay. If no music URL is set, play a quiet local WebAudio pad after the tap. Add a play/pause button that auto-advances the journey, a typewriter on the memory card at constant duration, and a reduced-motion path that keeps everything reachable. Greyscale palette, Archivo and Fraunces.
w-24:
Build a single-file HTML landing page in a greyscale register: no accent hue at all. Color, if any, arrives later from a client's brand or imagery.

Palette, all as CSS variables: ink #1D1D1F, secondary #515154, white, tint #F5F5F7, panel #EBEBED. Check text contrast: the secondary text must reach at least 4.5:1 on white, so do not use #86868B for body copy. System UI font stack for body, a large tight display size for headlines (clamp from 40px to 96px), light ground always.

Sections: a sticky top nav (wordmark and four anchor links), a two-column hero (headline "Grey, black, white. Nothing else.", a short lede, one solid and one ghost button, and on the right a swatch list showing each color, its hex and its measured contrast ratio), then Work, How, Numbers and Start sections that each use the same grid and one repeated card pattern.

Motion: elements with a .rv class fade up 24px as they enter the viewport (IntersectionObserver, 700ms, staggered with a --i variable). Nothing loops, no hover transforms. Use full width on a phone, with 16px minimum body text and 44px tap targets. With prefers-reduced-motion, show everything at once. Put every color and the CTA text in one settings block at the top of the file so they can be changed in one place.
e-07:
Build a single-file HTML pricing card, no libraries, centered on a light grey page (#F5F6F8).

The card is white, 460px max width, 12px radius, 28px padding, with a soft shadow. Content in order: a heading with the second half in italic serif ("One ticket. Everything included."), five itemized rows each with a name on the left and a struck-through price on the right (a guide, a skills library, a builder kit, a live session, a replay) with thin dividers, a mono uppercase summary row "BOUGHT SEPARATELY" with the total and a plus sign, the real price in large bold type (44px), a small mono terms line ("ONE PAYMENT, USD"), a full-width dark button "Register now", and a one-line risk reversal under it that tells the buyer what they keep either way.

The point of the design is concrete math in place of vague "value" claims: the rows must add up to the total shown. Button hover changes the background color over 200ms and nothing else moves. Use real numbers from the offer being sold; never invent a discount that was not offered. Body text at least 14px, tap target at least 48px.
g-01:
Build one HTML file that renders a social post in three sizes, chosen by a ?size= query: 45 (1080 x 1350), 11 (1080 x 1080) and 916 (1080 x 1920). Add a render script that screenshots all three at 1080px wide with a headless browser.

Look: monochrome print register. The top of the post is a public-domain line engraving from a museum open-access collection, bleeding off the edges and fading into ink with a printed gradient. Credit the source in small type on the image. Below it, a sheet in ink with a double rule, a tracked uppercase eyebrow (brand mark and "No. 01 - The System"), a Didot-style display headline, a one-line standfirst, and a numbered stage index: seven rows, each a tracked uppercase word on the left and its detail set in italic and right-aligned (BRIEF, RESEARCH, BUILD, WIRE, TEST, SHIP, WATCH).

Close with a fixed call to action block: a small kicker, a large keyword lockup, a short line telling people to comment the word to receive the full build, and a footer with the domain and city. On the 9:16 size keep all type below the top 200px so story chrome never covers it. All copy lives in one STAGES array and the headline and standfirst elements, so a new post is a copy edit. Greyscale only.
e-31:
Build a single-file HTML section, no libraries, one inline SVG.

Ground #F5F6F8, ink #1D1D1F, grey text #515154. Layout: a centered flex row that wraps, 56px gap. Left, a copy block (max 380px): a mono label "THE LADDER" (11px, bold, tracking .16em), an h1 "Every tier you climb compounds the last." (clamp 26 to 38px, weight 600, tight tracking), one grey line of about 34 characters, and a four-row legend, each row a 10px square swatch plus "Tier 4 running", "Tier 3 installed", "Tier 2 organised", "Tier 1 foundation".

Right, an SVG about 420px wide: a stepped isometric pyramid of four tiers, each tier made of three polygons (left face at brightness .96, right face at .87, top face at 1.05) in one hue. Tier colors from bottom to top: #E2E6ED, #C8D2E2, #9FB2D2, #5C7CB8. Above them sits a ghost capstone: two triangles with a 50% white fill and a 1.4px dashed #9FB2D2 outline, with a small solid padlock (#1D1D1F) in the middle. Solid tiers read as built, the dashed summit reads as gated on purpose.

Motion: each tier rises 18px and fades in over .7s with cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1), 0.18s apart from the bottom up, then the capstone fades in over .9s. With prefers-reduced-motion show the final state. On a phone, stack the copy above the SVG and make the SVG 80vw wide. Give the SVG role="img" and an aria-label that describes the four tiers and the locked cap.
e-30:
Build a single-file HTML article page, no libraries, one small script.

Colors: ground #F5F6F8, card #FFFFFF, ink #1D1D1F, grey #515154, line #E2E6ED, accent #5C7CB8. Column max 640px, centered, 56px top padding, system sans 16px/1.65.

Content from top: an h1 "The section everyone reads" (clamp 24 to 32px), one paragraph of real, readable text, then the gate: a white card (12px radius, 1px line border, soft shadow 0 12px 32px at 6% ink, 28px padding, centered text) with a small lock icon, an h2 "Get the download files", one grey line "Drop your email and the files unlock instantly", and a form with an email input (grey fill, 8px radius, min 220px) next to a dark button "Unlock". The form wraps on narrow screens.

Below the card, two more paragraphs of real content blurred with filter blur(6px), not selectable, not clickable and aria-hidden. The blur is the point: visitors can see there is more and roughly how much, so it converts better than a hard wall.

On submit, prevent the page reload, add a class to the body, transition the blur to none over .6s and hide the card. Button hover turns the accent color. Input font size is 16px on touch devices so iOS does not zoom. Use it for file downloads only, keep the page text itself readable.
e-32:
Build a single-file HTML section, no libraries, CSS animation only.

Colors: ground #F5F6F8, ink #1D1D1F, grey #515154, track #E2E6ED, accent #5C7CB8. A centered block, width min(640px, 90vw), system sans.

Top: an h2 "Where this gets you" (clamp 22 to 30px, tight tracking). Then a 6px pill track with 44px above it. A fill in the accent color grows from 0 to 70% of the track over 1.1s (ease cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1), .3s delay). At the end of the fill, 40px above the track, a dark tooltip (#1D1D1F, white mono bold 13px, 6px radius, small arrow pointing down) reads "4.5" and pops in .4s after the fill ends.

Under the track, six equal columns, each with a bold number and a mono 11px label: 1 Enquirer, 2 Starter, 3 Organised, 4 Owner, 5 Operator, 6 Self-driving. The fourth is in the accent color.

Below, one grey paragraph (max 52ch, 14px): the program stops at 4.5 on purpose, levels 5 and 6 are built on this floor, and naming the stop answers the "why not further?" objection and quietly advertises the next tier. Give the track role="img" with an aria-label that says the pointer sits at level 4.5 of 6. With prefers-reduced-motion show the end state. On a phone let the labels wrap and keep every label at least 10px.
e-34:
Build a single-file HTML hero, CSS only, no JavaScript. Load Instrument Serif and Inter from Google Fonts with Georgia and system sans as fallbacks.

Page black #000, text #f0f0f0. One full-height section, content vertically centered, inner column max 1100px with 40px side padding.

Background, three layers: two soft white radial glows (5.5% opacity at 72% across, 68% down; 5% opacity rising from the bottom edge), a ::before layer 20% oversized with two diagonal light streaks at 115 degrees (white 7% and 3.5%) shifted down 12%, and an ::after floor sheen over the bottom 45%.

Content: a pill "Announcing something new" with an arrow, 14px, dark 50% fill, and a 1px gradient border made with a mask (amber #f5c26b, green #7ee0a3, blue #7db6f7, pink #d78bd4, each at about 33% alpha, border drawn with mask-composite exclude). An h1 in two lines, "Headline for" then "your product", serif 400, clamp 56 to 96px, line-height 1, the second line in #9a9ea3. A sub paragraph, 18px/29px, #a1a4a5, max 520px. A button 40px high, 16px radius, vertical gradient #1b1c1e to #0c0d0e with an inset 1px ring at 14% white, label "Get started".

Phone: h1 stays at 56px, side padding 24px, the button is at least 44px tall. No animation needed, the light streaks are static.
e-18:
Build a single-file HTML long page, no libraries, vanilla JS.

Colors: ground #F5F6F8, panel #FFFFFF, ink #1D1D1F, grey #515154, line #E2E6ED. System sans 16px/1.6.

Content: five sections with ids s1 to s5, each min-height 92vh, padding 64px 8%, hairline bottom border, an h2 (clamp 24 to 34px) and a short paragraph. Titles: The problem, The system, What you get, Pricing, FAQ.

The bar: position fixed at the bottom, full width, white at 88% with backdrop blur 8px, 1px top border, 10px 4% padding, flex row with 6px gap, horizontal scroll allowed on phones. Five chips, each an anchor with a bold mono number and an uppercase mono label (11px, tracking .1em): 01 THE PROBLEM, 02 THE SYSTEM, 03 WHAT YOU GET, 04 PRICING, 05 FAQ. Inactive chips are grey with a transparent 1px border that shows the line color on hover. The active chip is a solid ink pill with white text, with a .25s color transition.

Behavior: an IntersectionObserver with rootMargin "-45% 0px -45% 0px" marks the section crossing the middle of the screen, and the matching chip becomes active. Clicking a chip scrolls to the section (smooth, instant under prefers-reduced-motion). One component does two jobs: it tells visitors where they are and lets them jump, which suits long sales pages. Keep chip tap targets at least 44px tall on phones and add padding at the bottom of the page so the bar never covers the last section.
e-22:
Build a single-file HTML component, CSS animation only, no libraries.

Ground #F5F6F8, card #FFFFFF, ink #1D1D1F, grey #515154, line #E2E6ED, success green #3E7A54. Everything in a monospace stack (ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas), 14px/1.7. Center the card on the page, width min(420px, 90vw), 10px radius, 1px line border, shadow 0 12px 32px at 6% ink, overflow hidden.

Header strip: three 8px dots in the line color, then the label "INSTALL.LOG" (11px, bold, tracking .12em, grey), with a bottom border. Body padding 18px 20px. Five rows, each with a green check and an uppercase step on the left and a small grey tracked label on the right: AUDIT week 1, SYSTEM CORE week 2, FIVE SKILLS week 2, SCHEDULED AGENT week 3, HANDOVER included. Then a dashed top border, 14px gap and a bold tracked status line "STATUS: YOURS IN 2 WEEKS" ending with an 8 by 14px block cursor that blinks (steps(1), 1s).

Motion: rows fade in and rise 6px over .45s, one every .35s starting at .2s, and the status line arrives at 2s. Under prefers-reduced-motion show everything at once and stop the blink. Give the card role="img" with an aria-label that lists the steps. This is a trust device: swap in your own five steps and timings, and keep them concrete.
e-23:
Build a single-file HTML component, vanilla JS, no libraries. Inter from Google Fonts with system sans as fallback.

Page black #000, text #f0f0f0, 64px padding. One panel, max 860px, centered, 16px radius, background #060607, inset 1px ring at 8% white, overflow hidden.

Top row (10px 12px padding, bottom border at 8% white): tabs Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go, cURL as 14px buttons with 10px radius; inactive #a1a4a5, active background #1a1b1e and text #f0f0f0. Then a flexible spacer and a right-aligned "Copy for AI" button in #a1a4a5 with a small chevron. The row scrolls horizontally on phones with the scrollbar hidden.

Body: monospace 14px/1.9, padding 22px 24px, min-height 180px, base color #7d8288, keywords #c6cacf, strings #d3c96f. Each tab shows a two or three line snippet that sends one message with an API key and a recipient, using an invented client library so no real brand appears. Clicking a tab swaps the snippet at once.

Make it a real tab widget: role tablist, tab and tabpanel, arrow keys move between tabs, Home and End jump. Make "Copy for AI" copy the visible snippet plus one line of instructions to the clipboard and show "Copied" for 1.5 seconds. Focus rings 2px white at 60%.
e-27:
Build a single-file HTML onboarding stepper, vanilla JS, no libraries. Space Grotesk for titles and Inter for text from Google Fonts, with system fallbacks.

Page black #000, text #f0f0f0, 64px 24px padding. A column max 760px centered. Four steps stacked vertically, each with 60px left padding and 56px bottom padding: "Create your account" (done, text "Done. You are in."), "Connect your data" (active, a button "Connect"), "Run your first job" (locked, a button "Run"), "Explore more" (locked, no button).

The rail: each step has a 19px circle at the left (2px border #63676b, black fill) and a 1px vertical connector at 8% white running down from it to the next step, hidden on the last step. Done: border and fill #3dd68c. Active: border #f0f0f0. Locked steps drop to 45% opacity. Titles 500 22px, body #a1a4a5 15px with 8px and 20px margins. Buttons: 40px high, 16px radius, vertical gradient #ffffff to #d9dbdd, black 600 14px text.

Behavior: pressing the active step's button marks that step done (green dot) and promotes the next one to active (full opacity, white ring), with .3s transitions. Only one step is ever active. Locked buttons are disabled and aria-disabled, and the active step gets focus after advancing. Phone: reduce the left padding to 52px. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by removing the transitions.
m3-01:
Build a single-file HTML button sampler in a Material 3 Expressive style, CSS plus a few lines of JS, no libraries. Use Roboto Flex from Google Fonts with system sans fallback, and Lucide icons as inline SVG (keep the ISC license note in a comment).

Tokens: surface #FEF7FF, on-surface #1D1B20, primary #6750A4 with white text, secondary container #E8DEF8 with #4A4458 text, container-low #F7F2FA, outline #79747E. Page max 1080px, 24px padding, an app bar with a shapes icon, the title "M3 Expressive, Sampler" and a round dark-mode toggle that swaps a data-theme attribute (use the matching dark palette: primary #D0BCFF on #381E72, surface #141218).

Sections, each with an h2 (24/32px): Buttons: a row of five 40px pill buttons (Filled, Tonal, Elevated with a soft shadow, Outlined with a 1px outline, Text), then a row with a Large (56px) filled and an Extra large (96px) filled with a sparkle icon. Connected button group: Day, Week, Month as tonal buttons joined by 2px gaps with aria-pressed, the pressed one filled primary and fully round. FAB and icon buttons: a 56px square-ish FAB with a plus, an extended primary FAB "Compose" with a pencil, and two round icon buttons (heart, star) that toggle.

Motion: while pressed, a button morphs from a full pill to a 12px radius and scales to .97, then springs back. Build the spring with a CSS linear() easing that overshoots slightly (about 450ms for shape and size, 280ms with no overshoot for color). State layers: 8% on hover, 10% on press. Focus ring 3px primary with 2px offset. Under prefers-reduced-motion remove the transforms and keep the color changes.
m3-01b:
Build a single-file HTML card and chip sampler in a Material 3 Expressive style, CSS plus a few lines of JS, no libraries. Roboto Flex from Google Fonts with system sans fallback.

Tokens: surface #FEF7FF, on-surface #1D1B20, variant text #49454F, container-low #F7F2FA, container-highest #E6E0E9, outline #79747E, outline-variant #CAC4D0, secondary container #E8DEF8 with #4A4458 text.

Cards: a grid of three (auto-fit, min 260px, 16px gap), each 12px radius, 20px padding, a 16px/24px weight 500 title and a 14px/20px body in the variant color. Elevated: background container-low with a layered shadow (0 1px 2px at 30% black plus 0 2px 6px 2px at 15%). Filled: container-highest, no shadow. Outlined: surface with a 1px outline-variant border. Copy: "Lifts on hover with a spatial spring; corners grow.", "Surface-container-highest fill, same motion grammar.", "Outline-variant border on plain surface."

Motion: on hover the card's corner radius grows from 12px to 28px and the elevated card lifts 2px. Use a CSS linear() easing that overshoots a touch for the shape (about 490ms) and a plain ease with no overshoot for color and shadow (about 285ms).

Chips: a row of four 32px chips (Springs, Shape morph, Variable type, Tonal color) with 8px radius and a 1px outline-variant border; aria-pressed toggles them. Pressed chips become fully round with the secondary container fill and no border. Chips are real buttons with 2px focus rings. Reduced motion: no transforms, color changes only.
m3-01c:
Build a single-file HTML controls sampler in a Material 3 Expressive style, CSS plus a few lines of JS, no libraries. Roboto Flex from Google Fonts with system sans fallback.

Tokens: surface #FEF7FF, on-surface #1D1B20, primary #6750A4, on-primary #FFFFFF, secondary container #E8DEF8, container-highest #E6E0E9, outline #79747E.

Switch: a 52 by 32px track, off state container-highest with a 2px outline border and a 16px outline-colored thumb; on state primary track and a 24px white thumb that moves right. The thumb travels with a CSS linear() spring (fast, about 450ms, slight overshoot). It is a real checkbox underneath, with a visible focus ring.

Slider: a 44px tall row. A 16px high pill track in the secondary container color, a primary fill with a 8px rounded left end and 2px right end, and a 4 by 40px rounded bar handle with a 6px surface-colored halo. Pressing the handle stretches it to 1.1 on Y with the same spring. Drive it with a transparent range input laid over the visuals so keyboard and touch work.

Wavy progress: an inline SVG 12px high with preserveAspectRatio none. A sine wave path, 4px round stroke in primary, clipped to 70% of the width and sliding sideways in a 1.1s linear loop; a flat secondary-container line for the remaining 30%; a 3px primary dot at the far end. Add role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow 70.

Below, a 48px loader: a primary square that rotates and morphs between rounded shapes on a 3.2s loop. Put a chip row on top (four toggle chips). Reduced motion: stop the wave, the loader and the springs.

Build a single-file HTML carousel in a Material 3 Expressive style, CSS only, no libraries. Roboto Flex from Google Fonts with system sans fallback.

Page surface #FEF7FF, text #1D1B20, 24px padding, max width 1080px, an h2 "Carousel" (24/32px).

The track: a flex row with 8px gap, overflow-x auto, scroll-snap-type x mandatory, hidden scrollbar, 8px bottom padding. Four slides, each flex 0 0 clamp(200px, 40vw, 320px), aspect-ratio 4 / 5, 28px radius, 20px padding, content aligned to the bottom, snap-align start. Each slide is a diagonal gradient with a white 16px/24px weight 500 label bottom left: Tonal purple (#6750A4 to #D0BCFF), Tertiary rose (#7D5260 to #EFB8C8), Secondary slate (#625B71 to #CCC2DC), Container (#4F378B to #EADDFF). A dark scrim (transparent at 40% down to 45% black) sits over the lower part so the label always reads.

Motion: on hover the slide's corner radius grows from 28px to 48px using a CSS linear() spring easing with a slight overshoot (about 490ms). The next slide peeks in from the right edge so people know to swipe. The track must work with touch, trackpad and keyboard (make it focusable and let arrow keys scroll). Under prefers-reduced-motion, change the radius with no transition.

Phone: slides are 70vw wide so one and a bit are visible. Add an aria-label on the track that says it is a carousel of four items.

Build a single-file HTML lead form that asks one question at a time, vanilla JS, no libraries. Everything is scoped under one root class with a unique prefix so it can be dropped into any page without style clashes.

Tokens (override on the root): page ground #F5F5F7, card #FFFFFF, ink #0A0A0A, soft ink #3F3F46, muted #6B6B70, border #E4E4E7, focus blue #1F6FEB, error #B3261E, an --accent that defaults to ink. System rounded font stack, mono for labels.

Card: max 560px, 16px radius, 1px border, shadow 0 18px 40px -20px at 10% ink, padding 28px 24px (36px 40px from 600px up), centered on the ground on a 16px gutter on phones. Top row: mono 11px tracking .14em eyebrow "ONE AT A TIME" and a "1 / 3" counter. Then the question as a big heading (30px, 24px on phones, weight 500, tight), one 56px field, and a full-width progress bar of three 6px pill segments that fill with the accent per step. Buttons: Back (hidden on step one), Skip on optional steps, and a solid ink Next at the right; the last step's button says Send.

Steps: 1 text "What do you need done?", 2 phone "What number should I send the quote to?", 3 four choice chips "How much is this problem costing you every month?". Rules: never more than one field on screen, validate each step with an error line in text (not only color), save a partial lead as soon as the phone is given, and end on a done screen with a fallback phone link if sending fails. Leave the submit endpoint empty so the demo posts nothing. Slides fade 200ms; none under prefers-reduced-motion. Enter submits a step. Set aria-live on the step change.

Build a single-file HTML service-site demo with a "few taps, then book" pop-up, vanilla JS, no libraries.

Host page: a plain landing page on #F4F5F7 with a white header, an h1 "Home repairs, done once and done right.", one grey line and a dark button "Get a free quote". Invented business name only.

The pop-up reads one JSON config block (a script tag of type application/json): brand name, a delay in ms, a booking URL, the steps (each a question plus 2 to 4 options with a label and a lowercase form of the label) and the result copy (title, body, button label). Behavior: it opens after about 1.5 seconds, only once per visitor (remember in localStorage under a key from the config), never on a page opened from a hash link, and never while another dialog is open. Dark card #12141C, text #F1F2F5, accent #F26A21 with dark text on it, max width 440px, 16px radius, over a dim layer at 62% black. A slim segmented progress strip on top, the brand in small caps, a close button, the question as a 18px heading and each option as a full-width 48px row with an arrow.

Flow: step 1 "What do you need done?" (Leak or burst pipe, New fixtures, Full renovation), step 2 "How soon do you need it?" (This week, This month). One tap moves on. The result names the answer: "We can inspect your leak or burst pipe for free", a body line, an accent button "Book a free inspection" that opens the booking URL with the answers as query parameters, and an optional "or call" link. "Look around first" closes it and leaves a small pill at the bottom left that reopens it.

Rules: no countdowns, no fake urgency. Escape and the dim layer close it, focus is trapped while open and returns after, role="dialog" with aria-modal. The card rises 18px and fades in over .5s; none under prefers-reduced-motion.
w-50:
Build a single-file HTML demo of a floating social button, vanilla JS, no libraries.

Host page: a plain #F4F5F7 page with a white header and one large h1 "Talk to us where you already are." Invented business name only.

The button reads one JSON config block (a script tag of type application/json) with a title, a side (left or right) and a list of links, each with a type (messenger, whatsapp, instagram, facebook, tiktok, youtube, x, email, phone) and an href. Only accept hrefs that start with https:, mailto: or tel:, and skip anything else, so a bad config can never inject a script link.

Look: a 56px round button fixed 16px from the bottom corner, accent #111 with a white chat icon and a shadow (0 10px 30px at 28% black). Tapping it opens a card above it: white, 18px radius, 8px padding, shadow 0 18px 50px at 22% black. It starts with a small 13px caption "Message us" at 70% opacity, then one row per link: 48px minimum height, 12px radius, a 22px icon and a 16px label (Messenger, WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Email, Call). Rows highlight at 12% grey on hover.

Motion: the card opens with a springy rise and scale (from 10px down and .92 scale, .42s, cubic-bezier(.34,1.4,.64,1)); the chat icon rotates and swaps for a close icon in the same spring. Hover scales the button to 1.06, press to .92. Escape, a tap outside or the button again closes it. Set aria-expanded and aria-controls, return focus to the button on close, make links open in a new tab with rel noopener. With prefers-reduced-motion remove all of the transitions.
